alert.short_description: Worker struck by Member of Public
key_details: On 26th February 2024, a Leading Hand (IP) attended an intersection of the project site due to a report
that a male resident had jumped on the side step of one of the Water Carts and had commenced abusing
the female operator. On arrival at this location the IP observed a male person (local resident) digging a
trench with a shovel across the width of one of the roads
The IP approached the male person and commenced speaking to him. As the IP spoke, the male person
has turned around, making threats of harm to the IP, and jabbing him in the chest with the handle of the
shovel. The IP swivelled on his feet attempting to avoid the handle, grabbing the shovel, and pulling the
shovel from the male persons grasp. As the IP has turned to speak to the male person he has received a
forceful blow to the left side of the jaw with a clenched fist.
The IP has staggered and both persons have fallen to the ground (male person on top) with the male
person attempting to further strike the IP to the face with clenched fists.
A nearby Traffic Controller has then intervened and dragged the male person off the IP. The male person
then returned to his residence shouting abuse and threats to project workers in the area.
The Police called to manage the Member of public. IP attended the medics and had a scan at the regional
hospital. IP required surgery to his jaw.
A formal ICAM investigation has commenced. Once completed, the lessons learnt will be
communicated/shared through a final Grey Banner Alert as soon as practicable.

alert.short_description: Vehicle rollover on journey from site
key_details: At approximately 4:00am on Friday 7 June 2024, a contracted Traffic Controller (Injured Person – IP) on
their rostered day off was travelling on a highway when they lost control, crossed two lanes of traffic and
rolled the vehicle on the verge.
The IP extracted themselves from the vehicle and made their way to the highway where two road trains
stopped and arranged assistance.
The vehicle emergency system alerted WA police (WAPOL), who attended the incident site and performed
alcohol and drug testing on the IP. Test results taken 2 hours after the initial incident showed that the IP
blew 0.023.
The vehicle speed tracker also showed that vehicle had been travelling at 152km/hr at the time of the
incident.
WAPOL called medics at a mine site, who deployed an ambulance to the incident location. The IP was then
conveyed to the mine site and assessed by Paramedics, before being flown to Perth for further medical
assessment and treatment.
The IP’s injuries are still to be confirmed, however, it is suspected to have sustained a fractured shoulder,
bruised or broken ribs and potential spinal injuries.

alert.short_description: Mobile Plant and Traffic Management Procedure Breach
key_details: On Saturday 20 January at approximately 0630, a Traffic Controller failed to present to work to set up the
Port Gregory Road, Northampton site to commence load and haul operations from a culvert. The
excavator that was supposed to be delivered to the site to conduct the works had also not been
delivered.
The contractor Site Supervisor then made the decision to commence works anyway.
The works were undertaken in a 110km/hr zone with no speed restrictions in place and no traffic
controllers on site. The excavator that was used to commence the works belonged to a local farmer who
agreed to assist.
The excavator had not been through a mobilisation/suitability assessment, it did not have a flashing light,
the operator was not wearing high-vis, and the operator had also not inducted or had seen/signed on to
the SWMS and Excavation Permit.
At approximately 0700, a Main Roads representative observed the works being undertaken without
adequate traffic management set-up or equipment. Works were stopped and the contractor
Representative was notified of the event.
A replacement Traffic Controller arrived at site at 0900, set up the traffic management devices and
reduced the work area to a speed of 40km/hr. The contracted excavator and operator also arrived at site
and works continued.
A formal ICAM investigation has commenced. Once completed, the lessons learnt will be
communicated/shared through a final Grey Banner Alert as soon as practicable.

alert.short_description: MoP driven through Vehicle Control Point colliding with TC and Fire Services
key_details: Main Roads was providing a manned Vehicle Control Point (VCP) for the Green Range bushfire road closure
at the intersection of South Coast Hwy and Cheyne Beach Road. The VCP was located east of the
intersection.
At approximately 19:55 a Member of Public (MoP) travelling westbound from the fire incident side of the
VCP has driven through the road closure point without stopping. The MoP collided with a Fire Services Fast
Attack Vehicle, and then struck a contractor Traffic Controller (TC).
The Traffic Control vehicle was parked on the left side of the road heading east (north side of the road) on
the shadow side of the closure signs, with flashing lights on; it was dark after sunset when the collision
occurred. The road section east of the VCP is straight on an improved section of road with good sight
distance.
The Fire Services crews on scene immediately called 000, requested assistance, and provided first aid where
possible. Police and Fire & Rescue attended the scene and extracted the MoP driver from their vehicle.
Injured persons were conveyed to the Albany Hospital, and the MoP driver transferred to Perth with head
injuries. The VCP point was relocated west of the intersection.
The TC was assessed at hospital, confirming right hand laceration/bruising and an ankle fracture; the
fracture was treated with a cast and no surgery was required. A second (uninjured) TC was escorted from
the scene to their home in Albany and accessed the contractor Employee Assistance Program (EAP) for
trauma counselling. Preliminary advice suggests the Fire Services Officer in the impacted Fast Attack Vehicle
sustained cervical spine injuries (details to be confirmed).
A WorkSafe injury notification has been made.

alert.short_description: Chain used for recovery of maintenance truck, snaps and recoils, smashing through mesh guard and windscreen
alert.road: Great Northern Hwy (approx 100km west of Kununurra)
alert.work_activity: Recovery of bogged flocon truck using chain attached to posi-track
alert.injury_type: No injuries — chain struck unoccupied vehicle
key_details: Maintenance crews were enroute to Warmun and had stopped to repair a pothole. As they pulled over on
to the road shoulder (approximately 100km west of Kununurra), the flocon truck has become bogged.
The crew made multiple attempts to reverse out of the bog, to no avail.
A check of the other truck and light vehicle confirmed that there was no recovery gear available, so the
crew have used a 10mm chain which was being used to lash down the posi-track. They've attached the
chain to the back of the posi-track and the front of the flocon truck and slowly moved forward to start
pulling the flocon out of the bog.
The posi-track was positioned approximately 6 metres from the flocon when the chain has failed under
the load, snapping, recoiling and smashing through the mesh windscreen guard and then the windscreen.
There was no one on foot at the time (one driver in the flocon, one in the posi-track and another
approximately 20 metres away in a light vehicle). Had there been workers on foot, this incident may have
had the potential for serious injury or fatality due to chain strike.
The crew abandoned the truck recovery and called the incident through to their supervisor. The
Supervisor then arranged for a heavy tow to be mobilised from Kununurra.
The tow truck arrived at the site at approximately 2:40 PM when recovery commenced. Both truck and
crews returned to Kununurra. An ICAM investigation has commenced.

alert.short_description: Traffic Controller sustains shoulder injury slipping on roadside batter
alert.work_activity: Setting up traffic management signage for road widening project
alert.injury_type: Left shoulder — slipped on soft batter, grabbed door and roll bar, felt pain
key_details: On Saturday, 11 April 2026, at 6:15 AM whilst setting up traffic management signage for a road widening
project, a Traffic Controller (TC) exited their vehicle on the passenger side. The TC's feet slipped out from
underneath them as they stood up on the soft batter at the shoulder of the road. In response to the slip,
the TC grabbed the door with their right hand and reached up and behind with their left to grab the roll
bar on the back of the Ute. They immediately felt pain in their left shoulder as they righted themself. The
TC completed the site set up however was unable to continue works due to the pain and reported it to
their crew leader.
First aid was administered, and the TC was taken to the emergency department for assessment.
Initial x-rays did not show any damage to the shoulder bones however further assessment with an
ultrasound is required. The TC was prescribed medication for pain and inflammation and deemed ‘unfit
for work’ for 2 weeks, resulting in a Lost Time Injury (LTI).

at the same time of day, the following morning.

documents.original_filename: Red Banner Alert - Preliminary Notice - 57935- Worker struck on shin with sledgehammer, resulting in a LTI- 15 April 2026.pdf

alert.short_description: Maintenance worker struck his shin with a sledgehammer, resulting in an LTI
alert.work_activity: Removing fallen tree branch from side drain at culvert face
key_details: Work crews were tasked with removing a large fallen tree branch in the side drain from the face of a
culvert to ensure adequate drainage. The crew had conducted a prestart and the crew leader had
assigned people to tasks.
The chainsaw operator had completed the top cut and bottom cut leaving a strap on part of the log to
prevent the cut piece rolling onto the chainsaw operator. The method chosen to separate the two pieces
was to place a wedge into the chainsaw cut and break the strap by hammering in the wedge.
The hammer operator (Injured Person – IP) positioned the wedge into the chainsaw cut then proceeded
to hit the wedge. The sledgehammer slipped off the plastic wedge and continued in an arc and struck the
IP on the shin.
The IP reported the injury to his supervisor and was then transferred to the hospital for assessment. First
aid applied included rest, ice and elevation. The IP was x-rayed and certified unfit for work for a day,
resulting in an LTI.
A formal ICAM investigation has commenced and will look at the use of the wedge vs completing the
cuts with the chainsaw. Once completed, the lessons learnt will be communicated/shared with the team
through a final Grey Banner Alert as soon as practicable.

alert.short_description: Truck rollover
alert.work_activity: Spreader truck transporting aggregate and towing float with multi tyre roller to pavement repair location
alert.injury_type: No injuries — driver confirmed no injuries after health check
key_details: A spreader truck was travelling westbound on South Coast Highway to a pavement repair location with a
partial load of aggregate in the truck body and towing a float with a multi tyre roller. As the truck came
around a corner at ~80km/h, the truck lost traction on the slick/wet surface of the road. The truck and
trailer slid sideways and eventually the truck flipped onto its side and the roller was thrown from the float.
Traffic management and supervisor arrived within 15 minutes. Traffic control was established. Heavy
vehicle recovery specialist arrived and commenced recovery. Drug and alcohol testing completed
(negative). Driver taken for health check and confirmed as having no injuries.
